column1: # The reference lane's disagreement classes, each with its owning plan item and a reason (plan W1.1: reasons are per
# (kind, spelling) class, or per kind with *, never per row). ReferenceLaneTest refuses a class with no row here.

column4: reason

the reference ranks the [0..1] overload (a PCT function with a body, isEmpty.pure:31) above [*] for a to-one argument; our catalog has only isEmpty(Any[*]) and our ranking does not prefer the closer multiplicity (reference-matching.md 7-10)
numeric-overload ordering: the reference prefers the closer numeric type (Integer/Float/Number families)
numeric and [1..*] overload families: the reference's parameter-by-parameter type-then-multiplicity ordering
numeric and [1..*] overload families: the reference's parameter-by-parameter type-then-multiplicity ordering
comparison overloads over [0..1]: the reference's multiplicity ordering
the reference's overload ordering (FunctionMatch: type first, then multiplicity, parameter by parameter; smallest wins) differs from both of our overload algorithms
our typer erases a TDS to the collection surface at typing time, so size binds to collection::size where the reference binds the TDS function (homework-2026-09-26.md §1)
an operator-span artefact: our parser's span for an infix run puts the call on a neighbouring operator's column
infix run splitting: a mixed run is split into different calls on each side
a different declaration chosen: the candidate rule (imports, core, Root) differs from the reference's
the declaration exists on one side only: our comparison natives carry lite-internal overload ids the reference's catalog does not declare (one declaration per id is W2.8's)
we type let as a node (TypedLet), the reference as a call of letFunction
the automap rewrite: the reference spells a dot over a collection as a map call; we type the member access directly
we type ^Class(...) as a node; the reference calls new(Class, String, KeyExpression[*])
we type ^$x(...) as a node; the reference calls copy
we fold Enum.VALUE to an enum literal; the reference calls extractEnumValue

forms typed as nodes, not calls (cast, if, eval, match, filter, project, getAll, colSpec, sort, ...), and calls our desugars rewrite before they are typed; W1.1's second push gives form nodes ids and spans so these rows can join
a qualified property we model as a function
a member read on the reference's side that is a call on ours: the arrow and dot spellings are not yet told apart (Member)
our typer inserts toOne where the reference's multiplicity rule accepts the argument as written
our typer inserts elementToPath calls the reference does not
infix run splitting: we type a mixed string run as more plus calls than the reference
a call of ours the reference has none for at that position: typer insertions, run splitting, and calls in bodies whose spans differ; each family is owned where its insertion is removed
